summary: Feed s139_double to IDS is degraded: 19.0% of TCP sessions are one-way (IDS requires bidirectional) and microbursts peak at 2.37 Gbps vs 1 Gbps port (237% overload). Both faults reduce IDS detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Broker/SPAN is forwarding only one direction for ~19% of sessions (24/126). Likely single-direction SPAN/mirror or TAP aggregation missing the return path / asymmetric routing with incomplete aggregation at the packet broker.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions for TCP reassembly and stateful signatures. One-way sessions cannot be reassembled, causing missed detections, false negatives, and evasion of stream-based rules.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow onto this single IDS feed so the IDS sees full handshake and bidirectional payload for stateful analysis.

findings.root_cause: Traffic microbursts of 2.37 Gbps in 1ms intervals exceed the IDS 1 Gbps ingress port by 137% (3 overloaded intervals). Packet broker egress queue or IDS NIC is dropping excess.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS is overloaded and will drop packets randomly during bursts, creating blind spots, missed exploits, and incomplete flow records despite needing full payload.

recommended_fix.why: Spread load across 2-3 IDS instances/ports with flow-aware hashing to keep each port <80% utilization and preserve complete sessions without drops.
